name: What is the typical timeline for building a detached ADU?

mainEntity.name: What is the typical timeline for building a detached ADU?

acceptedAnswer.text: The timeline for building a detached ADU generally ranges from 6 to 12 months, starting from initial design to final construction. This duration includes critical phases such as architectural design, securing necessary permits from local authorities, material procurement, and the actual construction process. Factors like project complexity, city review times, and material availability can influence the overall schedule. We work to streamline the process for efficiency.
acceptedAnswer.description: Building a detached ADU typically takes 6-12 months, covering design, permits, and construction, though project specifics can affect the timeline.
